title: Separate nested reusable trays
instruction: Separate the nested trays and place the orange tray upright on the left pad and the blue tray upright on the right pad.
context: Manual pack-out operators prepare containers for filling, including separating trays supplied in stacks. This prototype tests disengaging two physical lips between loose trays before staging the two trays independently.
setup: On the calibrated YAM station table (x forward, y left, metres), two free upright rectangular PETG trays are nested at x=0.265, y=0, with their long axes along x. The blue outer shell is 220 x 150 x 45 mm with 3 mm walls and floor, 240 g. It has two yellow 4 x 9 x 5 mm ledges protruding from its side walls and a right-side raised grip. The orange inner shell is 180 x 120 x 35 mm with 3 mm walls and floor, 170 g. Its two 4 x 11 x 4 mm side tabs are directly below the corresponding yellow ledges and its raised grip extends inward from the left rim. Two fixed green 254 x 203 x 3 mm mats lie flat at x=0.265 and y=+0.211 (left) and -0.211 (right). See reset.json for the complete dimensional layout. No randomization.
scoring: Final state, highest qualifying tier. A tray more than 50 mm below the table or a tab penetrating its ledge more than 2.5 mm on every box separating axis invalidates the trial. 0.25 for both tabs clearing the ledges horizontally. 0.5 once the trays have at least 2 mm clearance between their enclosing boxes. 0.75 if also both upright within 10 degrees. 1.0 if also entirely over their assigned pads, their low points within 2 mm of the pad tops, at least 30 mm between the trays, and both jaws at least 10 mm away. The full-score conditions must persist with at most 2 mm and 2 degrees motion over 20 consecutive control steps. Otherwise 0. Re-nesting loses separation credit.
reset_notes: Place both trays square at the center marks. Offset the orange tray along x to lower the tabs beside the outer ledges, then slide it back so both overlap. Clear both staging pads.
fidelity: Rigid PhysX compound colliders model the walls, grips, lips and tabs. The two trays are free independent rigid bodies and the lips obstruct direct vertical removal. Tray friction and mass are estimates. Polymer flex, wear and breakage are not modeled.
